target_customer: Indian online shoppers, mostly retail crypto users, who earn bitcoin cashback; brand partners who pay for rewards
problem: Indians who want bitcoin have little banking friction free access; GoSats gives bitcoin as cashback on everyday shopping instead of requiring users to buy it.
business_model: Affiliate and brand funded cashback rewards paid in bitcoin, plus card products
product_category: Consumer fintech, bitcoin and gold rewards

founders.name: Mohammed Roshan
founders.background_notes: A Hiro Stacker Chats interview calls him co-founder and CEO and says he got into bitcoin around 2014 and has built crypto projects with his sibling; education not found.

founders.name: Roshni Aslam
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; the interview says the two founders are siblings. Education not found.

competitors.name: Visa bitcoin rewards credit card (US)
competitors.what: A card that rewards purchases in bitcoin instead of cash or miles, announced for early 2021; a foreign analogue not an Indian rival

technical_complexity.rationale: Affiliate tracking, wallet and custody integration and a card launched with a payments network partner; mostly integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Affiliate relationships and a user base of bitcoin holders help, but the model is copyable and exposed to crypto regulation in India.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; Indian crypto exchanges faced layoffs and regulatory pressure in 2023, GoSats news did not show cuts.

market_need_then: India had fast growing e-commerce and many crypto users in 2021, but regulatory uncertainty around buying crypto made reward based accumulation attractive.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain rewards language, 'free bitcoin' pitch in the YC description

branding.brand_signature: Bitcoin cashback wheel and the cashback card launched on India's Independence Day (15 Aug 2021)
branding.community_and_virality: Reported 15,000 customers within six months of launch and over 700,000 users by October 2024 per search summaries (unverified against primary sources).

brand_strength.rationale: Name ties to sats (bitcoin units) and is easy to say, but no source explains it; coverage in Cointelegraph, YourStory and Entrepreneur India helped awareness.

outcome_analysis: GoSats raised a 700K seed in August 2021 and a reported 4M round in mid 2022, then a 5M Series A in April 2026, and remains active. It grew through a bitcoin cashback model in India and reported hundreds of thousands of users. Crypto regulation and tax pressure in India were headwinds that peers responded to with layoffs, but no cuts were found at GoSats.
notes: Seed 700K reported by YourStory and Entrepreneur India (two outlets); investor names come from a search summary. The 4M round of June 2022 is reported by Entrepreneur India; aggregators label it seed, Series A or pre Series A and disagree on investors (YC, Accel, Gossamer Capital named), so stage is other and investors left empty. Series A of 5M in April 2026 is reported by several outlets (Deccan Herald, CXO Digital Pulse, Entrepreneur India); one source says no lead was named while others say Konvoy led. Fetches of Deccan Herald and YourStory returned 403 so details come from search snippets. YC page says founded 2021, a search summary says 2019 or 2020, unresolved. The company site yielded only a tagline. Competitor entry is a foreign analogue; no dated Indian rival was found.
